scenes.title: 1972 Harvard Museum of Comparative Zoology: High-Investing Mother vs Brooding Pipefish Dad — Flip the Investment, Flip the Choosiness!
scenes.era: 1972, Museum of Comparative Zoology, Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1972 Harvard natural-history seminar gallery featuring two crisp museum-white **matte porcelain zoological sculptures** on oak pedestals — Pedestal A showing **Standard Maternal Investment (elaborate Peacock courting selective Peahen)** alongside Pedestal B showing **Male-Brooding Reversal (ornamented Female Pipefish & Jacana Bird courting a picky Brooding Father!)** — framed by a bold **Trivers Parental Investment Ledger ('Higher Care Cost -> Choosier Sex | Flip Who Broods -> Courtship Flips 180°!')**.

positions.who: Robert L. Trivers (mannequin in 1972 Harvard corduroy blazer and open-collar oxford shirt)
positions.where: standing between the two white porcelain zoological pedestals pointing from the brooding pipefish father sculpture to the flipped 'Male = Choosy!' column on the chalk ledger

positions.who: Two Harvard Biology Seminar mannequins (in 1972 knit sweaters holding field notebooks)
positions.where: leaning forward in 'Aha!' realization as the sex-role-reversed pipefish and jacana cases prove investment — not XY chromosomes — drives selectivity!

props.name: paired matte-white porcelain zoological sculptures (Peacock/Peahen vs Brooding Pipefish/Jacana Dad)
props.period_detail: stages Trivers's decisive sex-role-reversal proof cleanly per R46 porcelain-animal protocol
props.physical_behavior: visualizes the falsifiable core of Trivers 1972

props.name: Harvard Comparative Investment Ledger ('Mammals: Female Invests More | Pipefish/Jacana: Male Invests More | Long-Term Humans: Biparental Mutual Choice!')
props.period_detail: captures standard, reversed, and human biparental cases on one board

actions.verb_sequence: contrasts high-maternal-investment species on Pedestal A with male-brooding pipefish and jacanas on Pedestal B -> traces the 180-degree flip in who ornaments and who chooses -> adds long-term human biparental care where BOTH sexes invest and choose carefully!

reactions.reaction: nod amazed as one clean economic principle unites birds, reef fish, and human families
adds the 1971 Reciprocal Altruism & 1974 100%-vs-50% Sibling equations beside it

scenes.wardrobe: 1972 Cambridge academic attire: tan corduroy sport coat, oxford shirt, knit pullovers, and wool trousers.
scenes.lighting: Bright high-key Harvard museum tall-window daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Think courtship rules are wired rigidly to XY chromosomes? Meet pipefish and jacana dads who carry the eggs — the instant fathers pay the heavier parenting bill, dads turn picky and females compete for them!

key_visual.description: a sunlit 1972 Harvard comparative zoology gallery where Robert Trivers points between matte-white porcelain peacock and male-brooding pipefish pedestals beside a Parental Investment flip chart

layout.description: Sunlit study table with a matte-white porcelain reef grouper-and-cleaner-wrasse model and a Benefit > Cost Reciprocity chart.

positions.where: mapping how repeated encounters select for gratitude toward helpers and moral indignation at freeloaders

props.name: Reciprocal Altruism Payoff Card ('Cost Small, Benefit Large + Memory = Cooperation')

actions.verb_sequence: traces repeated favor exchanges -> highlights gratitude & reparative guilt as trust glue

reactions.reaction: sees human moral emotions as reciprocity software

scenes.recognition_hook: Why doesn't a giant reef grouper swallow the tiny cleaner fish swimming inside its mouth? Because tomorrow's parasite cleanup is worth far more than one tiny snack!

scenes.title: 1974 Parent-Offspring Conflict: 50%/50% Mom vs 100%/50% Kid!
scenes.era: 1974, Sunlit family kitchen & Harvard chalkboard (Trivers SRC2)

layout.description: Bright split view pairing a parent dividing slices equally (50% / 50%) between two children while Child #1 lobbies energetically (100% self vs 50% sibling!).

positions.where: acting out the universal sibling-fairness negotiation with warm humor

props.name: Relatedness Fraction Board ('Parent: 50% / 50% | Child: 100% Self / 50% Sibling')
props.period_detail: turns toddler weaning/sharing battles into crystal-clear genetics

actions.verb_sequence: divides attention 50/50 -> Child #1 lobbies for extra -> Parent smiles knowing the 2:1 relatedness math

reactions.reaction: replaces parental guilt with calm perspective

scenes.recognition_hook: Your kids aren't broken when they argue over fair shares — you're 50% related to both of them, while each kid is 100% related to themselves!
